name: Image Complexity
description: Highly complex images (e.g., many objects, cluttered scenes, low contrast) are more likely to cause both human and onboard classifier failures, leading to distinct, longer analysis times. This is the most likely driver as analysis difficulty fundamentally impacts performance.  We'd expect multiple groups – 'easy', 'medium', 'hard' images.

name: Object Class
description: The onboard classifier might perform significantly better on certain object classes than others (e.g., easily identifiable vehicles vs. subtle environmental changes). Human analysts might also struggle with specific classes.  Different classes will result in differing analysis times, causing modality.

name: Lighting Conditions
description: Poor or variable lighting (e.g., shadows, glare, low light) degrades image quality, impacting both human and classifier performance.  Distinct modes could correspond to 'good lighting', 'moderate shadows', and 'low light'.

name: Distance to Waypoint
description: UAV altitude/distance at the waypoint could impact image quality (blur, resolution) and thus analysis time.  Higher altitudes lead to lower resolution and potentially more errors.

name: Image Resolution
description: If resolution is not constant, lower resolution images are easier (and faster) to analyse but provide less detail, potentially leading to a different mode. Conversely, high resolution may expose more detail and increase analysis time.

name: Weather Conditions
description: Rain, fog, or snow reduce visibility and image quality, increasing analysis time or causing failure. Separate modes could represent clear, overcast, and rainy conditions.

name: Onboard Classifier Confidence Threshold
description: If the classifier has a confidence threshold, images falling just below it will be sent to the human. This creates a distinct mode around the threshold.

name: Human Analyst Fatigue/Attention
description: Human performance isn't consistent. Analyst fatigue or distraction could lead to slower or less accurate analysis, creating variability. Though hard to model directly, it's plausible.

name: Waypoint Type/Environment
description: Different environments (e.g., urban vs. rural, forest vs. open field) present different challenges for image analysis.  Rural scenes might have low object density, while urban scenes are cluttered.

name: UAV Orientation/Angle
description: The angle of the camera relative to the ground or object can affect image perspective and ease of analysis. Extreme angles can distort images.

name: Image Noise
description: Sensor noise, particularly in low light, affects image quality and analysis time. Different noise levels could contribute to distinct modes.

name: Communication Bandwidth
description: If communication bandwidth fluctuates, it can affect the time it takes to transmit images to the operator, creating a delay and influencing the observed time. This is less likely to directly cause *analysis* failure, but *total time* differences.

name: Time of Day
description: Correlated to lighting, but potentially has independent effects.  Early morning or late evening light could create specific challenges.

name: Target Object Size
description: Smaller targets are harder to detect, both for humans and classifiers. This may create a group of slower/failed analyses for smaller objects.

name: GPS Accuracy at Waypoint
description: Poor GPS accuracy could lead to images not being centered on the intended target, making analysis harder.  Less likely to cause distinct *modes* than the above.
